newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka prime minister in hospital for tests.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka prime minister in hospital for tests.

text.p: Sri Lankan Prime Minister Sirima Bandaranaike was being examined at a government hospital on Wednesday after she was admitted with a stomach ailment, doctors and officials said.
"The prime minister is being investigated for possible causes of her ailment," a senior doctor at Colombo's Sri Jayewardenepura hospital told Reuters.
"Doctors will decide on further action, perhaps tomorrow, after confirming the cause," said the doctor, who asked not to be identified.
Bandaranaike, who turns 81 in April, was admitted to hospital late on Monday. She was transferred to the hospital's special suite after spending one night at the intensive care unit, doctors said.
They said they were investigating the possibility of an ulcer in the prime minister's abdomen.
Bandaranaike earned a place in history when she became the world's first woman prime minister in 1960.

She became prime minister for the third time when the People's Alliance, led by her daughter President Chandrika Kumaratunga, won Sri Lanka's 1994 general elections. The role of prime minister is now largely ceremonial.

Frail and in poor health, she was last seen in public at last weekend's funeral of ruling coalition lawmaker Nalanda Ellawala, who was killed in election campaign-related violence on February 11. Local-level elections are set for March 27.
"Her condition is fine and she is meeting a limited number of visitors at her suite," said secretary to the Prime Minister Hemasiri Fernando.
